items.title: Anwar: Every early vote a trust to strengthen welfare of security personnel
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called on security personnel casting their ballots early in the Negri Sembilan polls to continue supporting the coalition's candidates. The prime minister said every vote cast would not only determine the direction of the state but also represent a mandate that his administration must uphold, particularly in safeguarding the welfare of security personnel and their families. PH and Barisan Nasional (BN) formed the Negri Sembilan government following the 2023 state election after securing a combined 31 of the 36 seats.

items.title: Nicky Liow not PKR member, says Fuziah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: PKR has denied businessman Nicky Liow is a member of the party following his appearance at a party event two days ago. Its secretary-general Datuk Fuziah Salleh said a check of the party's records found no indication that Liow, whose full name is Liow Soon Hee, had joined PKR. "I can confirm that Liow Soon Hee, also known as Nicky Liow, is not on the party's membership list.

items.title: Sombre farewell for six friends killed in Bentong crash
items.summary: TEMERLOH: A sombre atmosphere enveloped the cremation ceremonies as the remains of six friends who were tragically killed in an accident on Jalan Karak Lama in Bentong yesterday were cremated at two locations today. Kiisven were cremated at the Mentakab Hindu Crematorium, while K. Alaganathan, 21; A. Kanabati Raja, 19; and M. Paranthaman, 16, were laid to rest at the Sungai Kawang Crematorium in Karak, Bentong. Earlier, friends and relatives gathered at the victims' respective homes to pay their final respects.

items.title: [UPDATED] Ayob Khan calls for review of top police leadership structure
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Retiring Deputy Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay has proposed a review and realignment of the police's top leadership structure, saying it should better reflect the responsibilities and workload carried by the force. "If you look at it, the Inspector-General of Police is graded Turus 2, while the Deputy Inspector-General of Police is JUSA A. "The deputy should be graded Turus 3, followed by department directors at JUSA A and state police chiefs at JUSA B.

items.title: No Malaysians reported involved in Berlin attack - Embassy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: No Malaysians have been reported to be involved in an attack during the Christopher Street Day celebrations in Berlin, Germany, on Saturday night. This was confirmed by the Malaysian Embassy in Berlin on Sunday. The embassy also extended its sympathies to those who were affected by the tragedy, which left one person dead and at least 16 others injured.

items.title: Pavilion Reit set for higher rents after Parkson space revamp
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pavilion Real Estate Investment Trust (Reit) is expected to secure a significant rental uplift at Pavilion KL by November as new tenants move into space vacated by an anchor tenant, Kenanga Research said. The reconfiguration temporarily reduced Pavilion KL's occupancy rate to 91 per cent from 97 per cent. "We believe Pavilion Reit will likely secure significant rental uplift from the incoming tenants by November, given the low rental base previously enjoyed by the anchor tenant.

items.title: Mohamad: BN policies ensured aid for Negri Sembilan's vulnerable
items.summary: REMBAU: REMBAU: The social safety net introduced during Barisan Nasional's administration in Negri Sembilan was aimed at ensuring no citizen was left behind during tough times, says Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. The Negri Sembilan BN chairman said the policy was among his priorities when he served as menteri besar to ensure residents received immediate government aid when facing hardships. "My policy when leading Negri Sembilan back then was first and foremost the social safety net policy.

items.title: Ayob Khan: I wanted banking career, but friend persuaded me to join police
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Outgoing Deputy Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay today revealed that he never intended to join the police force, saying his original ambition after university was to pursue a career in banking. "I never had any intention of joining the police and was not interested in becoming a police officer. "I joined the police without any connections.

items.title: Bella, Syed Saddiq spark wedding buzz with bridal-inspired photos
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bella Astillah and Syed Saddiq Abdul Rahman have sparked social media speculation after sharing photographs in wedding-inspired attire, which netizens described as a pre-wedding shoot. "Every girl deserves her fairytale moment. "Looks like the date is getting closer," another wrote.

items.title: Ayob Khan: Integrity must start from the top, no room for police misconduct
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Retiring Deputy Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay today warned that misconduct within the police force would become entrenched if personnel involved in criminal activities were protected instead of being brought to justice.. Responding to questions on the recent arrests of personnel, including 12 policemen accused of extorting RM2 million from a Chinese national, Ayob said the force must take a zero-tolerance approach regardless of rank. he said.

items.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds forecast in parts of Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several states across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak until 6pm today. The affected areas are Langkawi in Kedah; Kinta, Perak Tengah, Kampar, Hilir Perak, Batang Padang and Muallim in Perak; Tumpat, Pasir Mas, Kota Bharu, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Bachok, Machang, Pasir Puteh and Kuala Krai in Kelantan; and Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus and Kemaman in Terengganu. In Pahang, the warning covers Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Raub, Bentong, Temerloh, Kuantan, Bera, Pekan and Rompin, as well as Hulu Selangor and Gombak in Selangor.

items.title: Integrity is the police force's greatest asset, says Ayob Khan in farewell message
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Retiring Deputy Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay left the police force with a simple but powerful message: never compromise on integrity, regardless of the circumstances. If you lose your house, you lose something. If you lose your character, you lose everything."

items.title: PM Anwar extends condolences to families of six killed in Bentong crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to the families of the six victims who were killed in a road crash along Jalan Karak Lama in Bentong, Pahang, early yesterday. In a post on X today, Anwar said he and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, were deeply saddened by the tragedy. “My condolences to all the victims’ family members.

items.title: Anwar extends condolences to families of Bentong crash victims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to the families of six victims killed in a road accident along Jalan Karak Lama in Bentong, Pahang. In a post on X today, Anwar said he and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, were deeply saddened by the tragedy. The 31-year-old lorry driver sustained serious injuries.

items.title: Ayob Khan retires as deputy IGP today after 35 years in police force, Ibrahim now acting DIGP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Outgoing Deputy Inspector-General of Police (DIGP) Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay today handed over his duties as he retires from the police force. In a ceremony witnessed by Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail at the Police Training Centre (Pulapol), Ayob handed over his duties as deputy IGP to Bukit Aman’s Special Branch director Datuk Seri Ibrahim Darus. Throughout his 35-year career, Ayob had held various positions before becoming the DIGP, including as head of Bukit Aman’s Special Branch’s counter-terrorism division, Johor police chief, Bukit Aman’s Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department director, and Bukit Aman’s Criminal Investigation Department director.

items.title: Typhoon Noul forces Malaysia Airlines to cancel flights to Shenzhen and Hong Kong
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Malaysia Airlines has cancelled several flights between Kuala Lumpur, Shenzhen and Hong Kong as Typhoon Noul brings severe weather to southern China, disrupting air travel across the region. The airline said services scheduled for July 25 and 26 — MH522 (Kuala Lumpur–Shenzhen), MH523 (Shenzhen–Kuala Lumpur), MH078 (Kuala Lumpur–Hong Kong) and MH079 (Hong Kong–Kuala Lumpur) — were called off due to deteriorating conditions linked to the approaching typhoon. Checks on AirAsia’s flight status page showed similar disruptions, with flight AK126 from Kuala Lumpur to Shenzhen cancelled on Sunday.

items.title: Rantau Panjang celebrates Aliff's historic ONE Championship triumph
items.summary: RANTAU PANJANG: Kelantanese, especially residents of Rantau Panjang, are celebrating hometown hero Ahmad Nor Iman Aliff Rakib's remarkable achievement after he won the ONE Championship interim strawweight Muay Thai world title in Bangkok on Friday. The Kelantan-born fighter stunned Thai legend Sam-A Gaiyanghadao with a fifth-round stoppage at Lumpinee Stadium, capping years of sacrifice and dedication to become Malaysia's latest world champion. "We are extremely proud of Aliff's achievement.

items.title: Umno must win urban seats to regain relevance, says Johari
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno must formulate a new strategy to regain support from urban voters after losing 10 of the 11 parliamentary seats in Kuala Lumpur, party vice-president Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said. Johari said Malaysia's changing demographic landscape, with a majority of the population now living in urban areas, required Umno to adapt its approach and strengthen its appeal among city voters. Because Kuala Lumpur has 11 parliamentary seats.

items.title: Knives, scissors thrown from apartment pierce restaurant canopy, nearly miss customers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Customers at a seafood restaurant in Pandan Indah had a close shave when knives and scissors thrown from an apartment building landed near them while they were having dinner last Tuesday. "Besides the scissors, about five or six knives were also thrown from the apartment building and found near the lake beside my restaurant. I then informed the apartment management before lodging a police report," he said.

items.title: Police hunting for Berlin Pride attacker
items.summary: BERLIN: Berlin police have published a picture of a 21-year-old man suspected of carrying out Saturday night's attack at the Pride celebration, in which a vehicle rammed into a crowd, killing one person and injuring more than a dozen others. the statement said. Police said the vehicle came to a stop in the central Tiergarten park.

items.title: UK's Burnham would call out Trump if in Britain's interest, he tells BBC
items.summary: BENGALURU: New UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham "will always put Britain's interests first", he told the BBC in an interview, parts of which were released on Sunday, when asked whether he was willing to call out US President Donald Trump. While Trump initially described Starmer's successor as "extremely liberal", he said this week he had a "very good conversation" with Burnham, who became Britain's seventh prime minister in a decade on Monday. The prime minister also said he would not call a general election before 2029.

items.title: N9 polls: Fahmi calls for focus on policies, not 3R or slander
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Pakatan Harapan (PH) has urged all parties contesting in the Negri Sembilan election to conduct mature campaigns by presenting ideas, policies and track records, rather than exploiting race, religion and royalty (3R) issues or spreading slander to win voters' support. "Political parties should compete through ideas, policies, track records and solutions to the people's problems, not by resorting to politics of hatred. PH has chosen to offer hope, not hatred," he said at a press conference at the Negri Sembilan PH main operations room here today.

items.title: Trader fined RM700 for selling contaminated sushi at Ramadan bazaar [WATCH]
items.summary: SETIU: A trader was fined RM700 by the magistrate's court here today after pleading guilty to selling sushi contaminated with harmful bacteria at a Ramadan bazaar. Khairul Fazlan Ab Aziz, 33, entered his plea after the charge was read before magistrate Iffah Nabihah Mohd Ishak. Khairul Fazlan was charged with selling ready-to-eat 'Sushi Miniroll Chicken Floss' contaminated with pathogenic microorganisms to an authorised officer at the Sungai Tarom Ramadan Bazaar in Bandar Permaisuri, Setiu, at 4.50pm on Feb 22.

items.title: Man arrested for repeatedly stealing money from mosque donation boxes
items.summary: SUNGAI BULOH: A man believed to have repeatedly stolen money from donation boxes at Masjid Bandar Baru Sungai Buloh (MBBSB) here was finally arrested yesterday. MBBSB manager Muhammad Faaez Khesim said police arrived just minutes after a report was lodged and detained the suspect. He said the suspect was believed to have stolen money from MBBSB donation boxes several times and was also linked to similar incidents in the area.

items.title: N9 polls: Cops open 14 election offence investigation papers as of Saturday
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Police have opened 14 investigation papers into election-related offences during the campaign period for the 16th Negri Sembilan state election as of yesterday, said state police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad. He said three investigation papers were opened yesterday under Section 435 of the Penal Code for committing mischief by fire, causing loss of or damage to property. "Cumulatively, from July 18 to 25, the Negri Sembilan Police Contingent received 28 reports related to election offences," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Senior police officers among 12 arrested in alleged RM2m extortion of Chinese national
items.summary: Citing unnamed sources, the newspaper said the victim paid US$140,000 (RM572,000) before later lodging a police report at the Dang Wangi district police headquarters. “He later came forward to lodge a report at the Dang Wangi District Police Headquarters (IPD). Dang Wangi district police chief Assistant Commissioner Sazalee Adam confirmed the arrests when contacted by Utusan Malaysia .

items.title: DPM Zahid: No one above the law if implicated in Tabung Haji RCI report
items.summary: TAMPIN, July 26 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has stressed that no one is above the law if their names are implicated in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). Ahmad Zahid, who is also Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said the RCI findings must be made known transparently, and if there are elements of wrongdoing, appropriate action can be taken according to due legal process. Asked whether the release of the report would affect BN’s campaign in the Negeri Sembilan state election, Ahmad Zahid, who is also UMNO president, said he did not think it would have an impact as people in the state are capable of making mature and wise assessments.

items.title: Probe into fake UNHCR cards, possible syndicate link in Kelantan
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Kelantan Immigration Department is probing suspected fake UNHCR cards found on three Rohingya men, amid efforts to determine whether the documents were linked to any syndicate. Its director, Garry Belayong John Siki, said the cases were the first involving suspected fake United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) cards detected by the department this year. Garry said the three Rohingya men were among 20 foreigners detained during Op Mega, a joint enforcement operation carried out in Kota Baru on Friday.

items.title: BN-PH deal not a lifelong contract, says Khaled
items.summary: PORT DICKSON: The agreement between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Pakatan Harapan (PH) to form the federal government should not be regarded as permanently binding, Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said. The Umno vice-president said the cooperation underpinning the unity government was forged to facilitate the formation of the federal administration following the 15th general election. The criticism stemmed from BN's decision to contest against PH and form an electoral pact with Perikatan Nasional in the state election, despite both coalitions remaining partners in the federal unity government.

items.title: University student remanded over newborn's body found at rubbish disposal area
items.summary: KUALA LANGAT: A university student has been remanded for four days to assist in the investigation into the discovery of a newborn baby's body in a hostel rubbish disposal area here. Kuala Langat district police chief Superintendent Akmalrizal Mohd Radzi said the remand order, which runs from yesterday until Tuesday, was granted to facilitate investigations under Section 318 of the Penal Code for concealment of birth. Police received a report from a man around midnight on Thursday regarding the discovery of the baby's body wrapped in cloth at the hostel's rubbish site.

items.title: BN-PN pact in Negri polls not a template for other states, says Sharkar
items.summary: KUANTAN: An Umno Supreme Council member has said electoral strategies adopted in one state should not automatically be applied elsewhere, as each state has its own political dynamics. "What happened in the Negri Sembilan election does not necessarily apply to other states. "Today, there are around 10 Malay-based political parties," he said.

items.title: [UPDATED] Ibrahim assumes duties as acting deputy IGP as Ayob Khan bows out
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay retired today after nearly 35 years of service in the police force, ending a distinguished career that saw him lead some of Malaysia's most significant counter-terrorism and criminal investigations. Datuk Seri Ibrahim Darus, the Bukit Aman Special Branch director, has assumed duties as acting Deputy Inspector-General of Police with immediate effect following Ayob Khan's mandatory retirement. Ayob Khan was appointed Deputy Inspector-General of Police on June 23, 2023, succeeding Tan Sri Razarudin Husain, who was subsequently elevated to the post of Inspector-General of Police.

items.title: Bukit Aman: Six to be charged over RM7m Petaling Jaya kidnapping tomorrow as two suspects become prosecution witnesses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Six men will be charged tomorrow over the RM7 million ransom kidnapping in Petaling Jaya after police completed their investigation into the case, while two other suspects have been released to become prosecution witnesses. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Comm Datuk M. Kumar said in a statement that the investigation paper into the case, reported on July 17, was referred to the Attorney General’s Chambers on July 24, which subsequently directed that charges be brought against the six suspects. The six are due to appear before the Petaling Jaya Sessions Court at 9.30am tomorrow.

items.title: Sabah Immigration denies viral claim of Filipino detainee deaths at depot
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, July 26 — The Sabah Immigration Department has denied a viral claim alleging that many Filipino detainees had died due to overcrowding at the state’s immigration detention depots. State Immigration director Datuk SH Sitti Saleha Habib Yussof said that the allegation was false, baseless and misleading. “All Filipino detainees housed at the Immigration detention depots in Sabah are in good condition while awaiting repatriation to their home country,” she said in a statement today.

items.title: Aminuddin challenges opposition to prove PH left development agenda unfinished
items.summary: PORT DICKSON: Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun has hit back at opposition leaders claiming they want to resume an unfinished development agenda under the Pakatan Harapan state administration. The Negri Sembilan PH chairman challenged his rivals to present factual evidence of any project or plan that had allegedly stalled during PH's five-year tenure leading the state. He was responding to Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who denied that BN was copying PH's manifesto, claiming instead that BN sought to continue a development agenda that had been interrupted.

items.title: German police hunt suspect after deadly car ramming near Berlin Gay Pride
items.summary: BERLIN: German police searched on Sunday for a suspect believed linked to Islamist circles after a car ploughed into a crowd near Berlin's Gay Pride celebrations, killing one person and wounding 16 others. A suspect, believed to have links to "Islamist circles" had been "identified" but not yet arrested, police spokesman Florian Nath said. "A vehicle entered the Tiergarten park and hit several people," police said.

items.title: Defence Ministry identifies asset procurements for G2G execution, says Khaled
items.summary: Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the approach would enable Malaysia to secure competitive pricing while providing greater assurance of supply. "Several countries, including Italy and France, have also proposed conducting procurement through G2G arrangements." Khaled said several criteria were applied in selecting Malaysia's G2G partners for asset procurements.

items.title: Ahead of 60th anniversary, King’s royal diplomacy elevates Russia-Malaysia ties, says ambassador
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — The royal diplomacy of Malaysia’s King, Sultan Ibrahim, has brought the people of Russia and Malaysia closer despite the geographical distance between the two countries, while elevating bilateral ties to a new sphere, Russian Ambassador to Malaysia Naiyl Latypov said. Praising His Majesty's royal approach, Latypov said the King's diplomacy has elevated Russia-Malaysia bilateral ties as the two countries prepare to mark the 60th anniversary of diplomatic relations next year. "Russia highly appreciates His Majesty’s royal diplomacy.

items.title: Former PM Muhyiddin says it should be PAS exiting Perikatan, not Bersatu
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Bersatu president Muhyiddin Yassin has pushed back against calls for his party to leave Perikatan Nasional (PN), arguing that PAS — not Bersatu — should be the one to step away from the coalition after choosing to end political cooperation between the two parties. FMT reported Muhyiddin saying said Bersatu, as a co‑founder of PN, could not be forced out of the coalition and retained every right to remain. PAS ended its cooperation with Bersatu early last month, though both remain PN components.

items.title: Mohamad Hasan says non-Malays have ‘no reason to be unduly worried’ by BN-Perikatan pact in Negeri Sembilan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Barisan Nasional (BN) has assured non-Malay voters they will not be sidelined if the coalition secures victory in the upcoming Negeri Sembilan state election, despite its cooperation with Perikatan Nasional (PN). According to The Star , BN deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said claims by rivals that minorities would be marginalised were unfounded, stressing that BN remained the dominant force in the partnership. He added that seven of BN’s seats had been allocated to MCA and two to MIC, while PN was also fielding non-Muslim candidates.

items.title: Malaysian students breathe easier as Australia spares Asean neighbours from visa fee surge
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Australia has imposed a sharp 25 per cent rise in international student visa fees but carved out an exemption for applicants from Asean nations, including Malaysia, as part of efforts to deepen regional ties. “A reduced visa fee rate for students from Asean nations reflects the importance Australia places on welcoming high quality students from South-east Asia,” Assistant Minister for International Education Julian Hill told Singapore’s The Straits Times (ST). Australia already applies lower fees for Pacific nations, including Timor Leste, which joined Asean in October 2025, as part of its diplomatic outreach.

items.title: Nadma: Disaster victims can claim cash aid up to four times a year
items.summary: JERTIH, July 26 — Malaysians affected by disasters are eligible to receive the Bantuan Wang Ihsan (BWI) up to four times a year, subject to the claim conditions set by the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma). Nadma Community and Social Development Section director Jefny Muhammad said the assistance is provided to ease the burden of victims affected by disasters such as floods, landslides, fires, tidal waves and other calamities. Jefny said 108,000 heads of household nationwide received BWI amounting to RM108 million during the 2025/2026 Northeast Monsoon season.

items.title: Housewife loses RM119,599 to Facebook investment scam
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, July 26 —A housewife lost RM119,599.24 after falling victim to an investment scam on July 19. Kota Tinggi police chief Supt Yusof Othman said the 58-year-old woman came across an advertisement for an investment scheme, identified as XM Royal, on Facebook. Yusof said the victim realised she had been scammed after failing to receive the promised investment returns despite making several payments.

items.title: Temporary shelters house families in flood-stricken Melaka Tengah and Jasin
items.summary: MELAKA, July 26 —The number of flood victims in Melaka rose to 124 people from 37 families as of 8 am today, with three temporary relief centres still operating in Melaka Tengah and Jasin. In Melaka Tengah, 55 victims from 17 families are taking shelter at the Pantai Kundor Japerun Hall. while 44 victims from 12 families are placed at SK Serkam Darat and 25 victims from eight families at SK Bukit Tembakau in Jasin.

items.title: Scammer poses as government official, contractor loses over RM50,000
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, July 26 — A 52-year-old electrical wiring contractor lost RM50,400 after falling victim to a fake government tender offer scam. Kuala Terengganu police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the victim received an email on July 14 containing a quotation request for the installation of solar LED street lights purportedly under a special local authority allocation. “The victim, who believed the offer was genuine, made two payments totalling RM50,400 to two separate bank accounts on July 23 using business funds.

items.title: PM Anwar attends Citrawarna 2026 launch and cultural parade
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim attended the opening ceremony and parade of Citrawarna 2026 at Dataran Merdeka yesterday, a flagship Tourism Malaysia event held as part of the Visit Malaysia 2026 (VM2026) campaign. He was joined by Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing, Deputy Minister Chiew Choon Man, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Tourism Malaysia director-general Mohd Amirul Rizal Abdul Rahim. Supported by Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL), Warisan Kuala Lumpur, the National Department for Culture and Arts (JKKN), Istana Budaya and the National Textile Museum, Citrawarna 2026 aims to promote Malaysia’s arts, culture and heritage tourism to domestic and international visitors.

items.title: Police detain man for assaulting Ipoh officer issuing compound notice
items.summary: IPOH, July 26 — Police have detained a man to assist investigations into an incident in which an Ipoh City Council enforcement officer was assaulted and threatened while issuing a compound notice at Jalan Pengkalan Barat 35 yesterday. Ipoh district police chief ACP Muhammad Najib Hamzah said the 42-year-old suspect allegedly acted aggressively by trying to hit the officer with a vehicle, tailing him, pulling his shirt collar and making threats. “Acting on information, a team of officers from the Ipoh District Police Headquarters Criminal Investigation Department detained the suspect today at about 12.40 pm to assist investigations.

items.title: Raja Muda of Selangor, wife, welcome first child, Tengku Alia Amira
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, July 26 — The Raja Muda of Selangor, Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah and his wife Datin Paduka Seri Afzaa Fadini Abdul Aziz yesterday announced the birth of their first child, Tengku Alia Amira Tengku Amir Shah. Tengku Amir Shah and Datin Paduka Seri Afzaa Fadini were married in a royal solemnisation ceremony at Masjid Istana Diraja, Istana Alam Shah, Klang, on Oct 2, 2025. The royal couple was solemnised by Selangor Mufti Datuk Dr Anhar Opir, witnessed by Tengku Panglima Raja Selangor Tengku Ahmad Shah Alhaj and Tengku Indera Pahlawan Diraja Tengku Datuk Setia Putra Alhaj in the private wedding ceremony.

items.title: BN chairman defends manifesto as original and improved, dismisses ‘copying’ accusations
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, July 26 — Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has rejected allegations that BN’s manifesto, launched yesterday, was copied from those of other parties. The Umno president said the manifesto built on BN’s existing agenda and had been refined to meet current requirements. Early voting for the Negeri Sembilan state polls will take place this Tuesday, with polling day scheduled for Aug 1.

items.title: Third flood relief centre opens in Melaka as number of evacuees rises
items.summary: MELAKA, July 26 — The third temporary relief centre has been opened in Melaka to accommodate the increasing number of flood victims as of 8 pm yesterday. The Melaka State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said the third relief centre opened is at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Bukit Tembakau at 3.15pm yesterday. Three areas in Jasin are affected, namely Kampung Pulai, Kampung Serkam and Kampung Bukit Tembakau.

items.title: PM Anwar demands swift action on Felda initiatives amid settler frustration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants the seven initiatives announced earlier to help Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) settlers implemented without further delay. Anwar said he has requested progress reports on all initiatives, which include assistance to Felda and new generation housing, to be provided every month so that their implementation is not delayed. On July 7, the Prime Minister announced seven initiatives in conjunction with Felda Settlers’ Day and 70th Anniversary celebration, including strengthening digital literacy for settlers involving an allocation of RM15.85 million to 317 eligible Felda schemes.

items.title: Malaysians in Qatar urged to follow security advisories, avoid military areas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Malaysians in Qatar have been advised to follow security instructions issued by the local authorities and avoid military areas following the latest developments in the Gulf region. The Embassy of Malaysia in Doha also urged Malaysians to remain vigilant, stay alert to their surroundings, and avoid being influenced by or spreading false information and rumours. The embassy also advised Malaysians to check the latest flight schedules before travelling from Qatar and to ensure their personal and family information are kept up to date.

items.title: Perikatan launches Negeri Sembilan election manifesto with six main pillars
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 26 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) today launched its manifesto outlining six main pillars for the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election. The manifesto, with the theme ‘PN Sepakat Hebatkan Negeri Sembilan’, was launched by PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar. For the latest updates on the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election, visit https://prn.bernama.com/n9.

items.title: For nearly a century, this Penang family in Jelutong has let the sun make its soy sauce
items.summary: Today, brothers Kam Kam Yoon, 87, and Kam Pak Yuen continue running San Kwan Loong Soy Sauce Factory using the same natural fermentation method their mother brought from China when the family business was established almost 100 years ago. “We still make our soy sauce using natural fermentation under the sun,” he said. Kam Kam Yoon took over the San Kwan Loong soy sauce factory business at 19 years old.

items.title: Three secondary school students in Ampang detained over bullying incident
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Police have arrested three male secondary school students near here on suspicion of beating another student at a block of flats in Ampang. Ampang Jaya District Police Chief ACP Khairul Anuar Khalid said that during the incident at 12.31 pm yesterday, the victim was taken to the bottom of a staircase at a block in Flat Sri Nilam, Ampang, by a male student before being struck on the face and body by the suspects. Earlier, a 3-minute and 29-second video showing a male student being beaten by another student went viral on social media, having been filmed by a third individual.

items.title: Autistic girl dies in 13th-floor apartment fall in Kuala Terengganu
items.summary: Kuala Terengganu police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the department received a call around 7.50 am reporting a young girl lying in the sixth-floor parking area, believed to have fallen from a 13th-floor window. “The victim was pronounced dead at the scene by a medical officer from Hospital Sultanah Nur Zahirah (HSNZ),” he said in a statement today. He said the victim’s mother realised her daughter was missing only after another resident informed her at around 7am.

items.title: Anwar says there is a need to reconstruct history to the Malaysian narrative
items.summary: He said history must not be dictated by the country’s former colonial masters, whether it is the United Kingdom, Japan or the United States. “It must be determined by our people and reconstructed to give meaning to the level of sacrifice and devotion of the people of Penang,” he said at the official opening of Fort Cornwallis after restoration works on the colonial monument. He said it is not necessarily erasing history but a fact that there is a different narrative behind the monuments left behind by the country’s former colonial masters.

items.title: Education groups Dong Zong and Jiao Zong decry PAS president Hadi Awang’s ‘pendatang’ remarks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Two of Malaysia’s largest Chinese education advocacy groups, Dong Zong and Jiao Zong, have issued a strong joint condemnation of PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang’s recent remarks labelling DAP supporters as “pendatang” (immigrants) and accusing some Malay Muslims of being “ungrateful” and “colluding” with others. In a joint statement released today, the duo—collectively known as Dong Jiao Zong—warned that such rhetoric undermines the national identity by defining citizenship along ethnic and religious lines, while distorting healthy political competition into inter-ethnic hostility. They said the remarks not only fail to strengthen national unity but also risk eroding the longstanding trust built among Malaysia’s diverse communities.

items.title: Former PM Najib undergoes coronary procedure; no stent needed, doctors confirm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Former Malaysian Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak is in stable condition and recovering after undergoing a coronary angiogram today, with doctors confirming that no further surgical intervention, such as balloon angioplasty or stent implantation, is required. According to a statement released by his legal counsel, Messrs Shafee & Co., the medical procedure was deemed necessary following a series of health evaluations over the past several weeks. The medical team had previously advised that there was an estimated 95% probability that Najib would require further intervention.

items.title: Police launch 16 probes into alleged election-related offences in Negeri Sembilan
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 25 — Negeri Sembilan police have received 16 reports and opened 11 investigation papers, including two opened yesterday, over alleged election-related offences in the state polls. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said one investigation paper opened yesterday was under Section 435 of the Penal Code for committing mischief by fire, resulting in the loss or damage of property. However, Alzafny said the security and public order situation throughout the election process remained good and under control.
